To make the chermoula aÃ¯oli, place the egg yolks and Dijon mustard in a mixing bowl and whisk while slowly pouring in the oil. Keep whisking until the oil-and-yolk mixture has increased in volume and turned pale in colour. Add the lemon juice and season to taste. Add the remaining ingredients and combine. Serve with the grilled yellowtail.
Place thick slices of ciabatta under a hot grill then toast on both sides until golden.
Serve on a large platter, generously spread with Duetto Dolce and topped with fig spread or green fig preserve.

ing: A bunch Watercress, large stalks removed
1/2 Medium-sized onion, chopped into fine brunoise
sea salt and freshly ground pepper, to taste
60 g Grana Padano cheese, plus extra for serving
st: Place a thick-bottomed pan over a medium heat then add the olive oil and rice.
Slightly sautÃ© the rice over a low heat.
After a minute, add the chopped onion and garlic. Stir continuously with a wooden spoon, controlling the heat to make sure the mixture does not start to discolour.
After 2 minutes, deglaze the pan with the vermouth and continue stirring. Add the white wine after the vermouth has been completely absorbed. Continue stirring.
In a separate pan, heat the chicken stock, but do not allow it to boil.

Add a ladle of chicken stock to just cover the rice then continue stirring, allowing the risotto to cook slowly, but not on the lowest heat (the rice needs to absorb the stock while the latter slowly bubbles away).
After adding a third ladle of stock, the rice should have swollen significantly.
Continue cooking until al dente, but not raw. Add one more ladle of stock then reduce by half, ensuring that the rice remains moist.
Remove from the heat, add the Gorgonzola, freshly grated Grana Padano, freshly grated nutmeg and butter, and fold in the watercress. Season.
Slowly stir the risotto to incorporate all the ingredients â you should be left with a creamy textured risotto.
Sprinkle with pine nuts, a few extra sprigs of watercress and grated Grana Padano.

ing: 3 bunches Watercress, roughly chopped, plus extra for serving
sea salt and freshly ground pepper, to taste
st: Preheat the oven to 200ÂºC.
Line a 5cm x 17cm loose-bottomed sandwich tin with the pastry (or use a similar tart ring placed on buttered greaseproof paper on a baking sheet).
Prick the base then chill. Cut out a disc of greaseproof paper, about 1cm shorter than the diameter of the tin, then grease on one side.
Beat the eggs with the cream, mascarpone and some seasoning then set aside.
Fry the spring onion in a dab of butter until softened, but not coloured, then stir in the garlic.
Fold in the chopped watercress and allow to cook until slightly wilted. Remove from the heat then fold in the chopped herbs.
Pile this mixture into the pastry-lined tin then pour in the egg mixture and cover with the greased disc of paper (buttered side down).
Place on a baking sheet and bake on the middle shelf of the oven for 40 minutes, or until the egg has just set.
Remove from the oven, discard the buttered paper and allow to cool a little before removing from the tin.
Top with freshly snipped watercress and serve.

ing: sea salt and feshly ground pepper
st: In a blender, combine the olives with the olive oil and parsley to form a loose paste.
Spread the paste on the pita breads and pile on the radish, watercress, eggs and chives.
Season to taste.

t: Green beans with a maple dressing
ing: 350 g Fine green beans, tops and tails trimmed
st: For the dressing, put all the ingredients into a small saucepan over a medium heat. Simmer for 1 â 2 minutes until the dressing has a creamy consistency. Set aside.
Steam the green beans for 5 â 6 minutes or until tender. Drain and set aside.
Place the beans into a serving dish and drizzle with the coconut and maple dressing.
To serve, sprinkle the toasted almonds and pomegranate seeds over the beans.

ing: sea salt and freshly ground pepper, to taste
st: Preheat a pan to high
Toss the asparagus with the olive oil and grill, turning them for 3-4 minutes or until bright green and tender. Transfer to a bowl.
Cook the peas in a saucepan of salted water, then drain and add to the asparagus.
For the dressing, comine the red pepper, onion, lime juice, olive oil, mint and sugar in a bowl. Mix well and season with salt and pepper.
Drizzle the dressing over the asparagus and peas, and toss to combine.
Arrange on a serving platter and serve.

t: Farmed kob in spicy tomato ragÃ¹
ing: pinch each salt, sugar & black pepper
600 g farmed kob or sustainable firm white fish, filleted into 150g portions
st: Heat the oil add garlic and fry until golden brown.
Briefly brown the seasoned fish in the hot oil, only for about 1 minute then remove and set aside.
Add the tomatoes and stir.
Cook the sauce for about 20 minutes and adjust seasoning with salt and sugar. The sauce should reduce and thicken at this stage. Add the chopped basil.

Place the fish back in the sauce and cook on a low heat for about 5 minutes, until the fish is just cooked. Donât cover the fish with sauce â retain the red, white and green colours for aesthetics.
To serve, dish the ragÃ¹ in a serving plate first, then the fish on top and garnish with basil leaves and drizzle with chilli oil.

ing: 1 bouquet garni (bay, parsley, thyme, black pepper)
st: Cut all your vegetables into rough blocks. Warm the oil in a large pot and sautÃ© your vegetables, making sure that they soften, but donât colour.
Top up with cold water and add the bouquet garni.
Bring to the boil and reduce the heat to a simmer. Continuously skim the stock.
Simmer for about 30 minutes.
Strain though a fine sieve, discard the vegetables and cool the stock, before storing it in the refrigerator.
The stock can be reduced by two thirds and frozen in ice trays for general use in all cooking.

ing: 1 bouquet garni (bay, dill, parsley black pepper)
st: Add the oil to a large stockpot.
Add the onion celery and carrots, and place the bones on top.
Sweat the vegetables and bones over low heat for about 5 minutes, until the bones turn opaque and release some juices.
Deglaze with the 250ml water or white wine and bring to a simmer.
Add the bouquet garni and cold water to cover.
Bring to a simmer, skim any scum that forms, and continue to simmer for 25 minutes.
Strain through a fine sieve or a sieve lined with muslin cloth.
Cool the stock immediately in an ice-water bath, transfer to a container and refrigerate.
Skim off any fat that rises to the top.
Store in the freezer until needed. This makes a great base for soups and fish stews.

t: Green olive and dried apricot salad
ing: 80 g crumbly reduced fat feta cheese
1/2 small red chilli, seeded and finely chopped
2 tbsp flat leaf parsley, finely chopped
130 g red pepper, roasted, skinned and chopped
40 g pistachio nuts, roasted and chopped
35 g walnuts, roasted and finely chopped
80 g green olives, pitted and finely chopped
st: To save some time you can chop the ingredients in a food processor but every ingredient on its own.  Pulse it â a little at a time otherwise it easily turns into a puree.
Mix everything together and let it stand for at least one hour before serving. It is almost better the next day.
Serve with yoghurt and tandoori turkey.
Seed and finely cube the tomatoes.
Thinly slice the spring onions at an angle.  Place in the same bowl as the tomatoes along with the deseeded chopped chilies.
Roughly chop the coriander so that the leaves are still rustic and add to the bowl. Add olive oil and lemon juice and give a stir.   Season with salt and pepper.
Slice each calamari tube in half and carefully score lines into the inside to ensure the tubes curl up when placed in the pan.
In a bowl, place lemon zest, deseeded chopped chilli, calamari, olive oil and black pepper. Allow to marinate for about 20 minutes.
Heat a pan and add seasoned calamari in a single layer to the pan.
Cook briefly for about 1-2 minutes each side.  The tubes will curl up and have a bit of colour, but should not be brown and tough.
Serve calamari warm with the tomato sambal.

ing: 150 g Chopped dried fruit, figs, apricot, apple or fresh fruit like berries
st: Whisk the eggs, oil and sugar together in a large bowl.
Add the remaining ingredients and mix until well combined.
Store in an airtight container in the fridge.
To bake, pre-heat the oven to 180Â°C.
Grease the muffin pan well and fill each hole about two thirds with the muffin mixture.
Bake for about 20-25 minutes.
Remove from the tray to allow them to cool down.

ing: Cook 'n Bake Original Non-Stick Cooking Spray
st: Place the dates in a food processor and blend until smooth, and paste-like.  Add the coconut and blend for 30 sec until combined.
Remove date mixture from the blender and line the base of a 20cm tart tin.  Place in the fridge until needed.
Chop your dark chocolate very fine.
Place the milk in a pot in on the stove and bring to the boil, then pour over dark chopped chocolate and let it melt.  Allow the chocolate milk to cool.
Whisk your eggs and add slowly to chocolate mixture, mixing well after each addition.
Take tart tin out of the fridge and pour dark chocolate mixture into it.
Bake in the oven on 155Â°C for 30 minutes.
Check tart after 25 minutes.
Remove from the tin and decorate with fresh berries just before serving.

ing: 2 large baby marrows, quartered and cut into 4cm lengths
4 sustainable fish fillets (farmed kob or rainbow trout)
st: Heat the grill of the oven
Add the tomatoes, olive halves and baby marrows to a roasting tray and drizzle with the olive oil. Lightly season. Add the lemon wedges
Grill the vegetables for about 5-10 minutes until they soften, then push them to the sides and place the seasoned fish fillets in the middle.
Grill for a further 5-7 minutes until the fish just starts to flake.
Add the capers, garnish with basil and serve. (Hot lemon juice should be squeezed over the fish.)
Pre-heat oven to 180ËC.
Place onions, lemongrass, garlic, chilli, ginger, lime leaves, turmeric, tamarind and oil into a food processer and blend as fine as possible.
Take the coconut flakes and spread them on an oven tray and roast in the oven until golden brown.  Remove from the oven and set aside until needed.
Coat each portion of fish with a thin layer of the curry paste and allow it to marinate for about 20 minutes.
Change the oven setting to grill and place the fish portions in a greases roasting tray.
Place the tray under the grill (not too close to the heat) and cook for 5-10 minutes, just until the fish starts to flake.
Serve the fish garnish with the toasted coconut flakes.

ing: 4 tbsp Slimmerâs Choice mozzarella cheese, grated
st: Pre-heat oven to 170ËC.
To make the crust place finely shred the cauliflower in a food processer, then steam until soft. Set aside and allow to cool.
Stir the cheese, thyme and egg into the cauliflower mixture and press the mixture into a deep quiche tin.  Wet hands are very helpful when doing this task.
Place the crust in the fridge to chill for 30 minutes, then place the tart tin in the oven and bake until pastry case is set.
Slice leeks in half lengthwise then cut into 0.5cm slices wash very well and drain on paper towel.  Place a pan on the stove add the olive oil and sautÃ© until al dente.
Slice portabellini and large exotic mushrooms into 1cm slices and add to the leeks. Also add the thyme. Trim and add the smaller exotic mushrooms whole.
SautÃ© the mushrooms to golden brown and donât steam them.
Clean and wash the Swiss chard and tear into large pieces. Add the Swiss chard to the mushrooms and sautÃ© until just wilted.
Spread the filling evenly into the tart case.
Crack the egg yolks into a bowl, add the milk and whisk very well.  Season with salt and pepper then pour over the mushroom and Swiss chard filling.
Place in the oven and check after 30 minutes to make see if it is ready. If it is getting too brown cover the tart with foil until the custard is set.
This tart can be served hot or at room temperature.
Wash and trim the bases of the Brussel sprouts.

Bring a pot of seasoned water to the boil and add the Brussel sprouts. Cook for about 10 minutes, then remove the sprouts and refresh in ice water. Drain, dry and cut the Brussel sprouts in half then dress with the olive oil.
Warm a grill pan and grill the sprouts for a minute to give them good colour. Place in a bowl and keep hot as you grill the rest.
(You can also roast them under a hot grill on a baking tray.
Combine the lemon juice, lemon oil and zest and briefly dress the Brussel sprouts in the bowl, when they are piping hot, then move them onto a hot serving platter.
Garnish with the toasted almonds and cheeks of lemon.

ing: 1 large red pepper, roasted, seeded and skinned
110 g red chillies, medium hot and seeded
st: Chop the chillies roughly and place in a food processor with the garlic.
Grind the toasted spices in a spice grinder or mortar and pestle and add to the chillies with salt and fresh coriander. Pulse until roughly chopped, and then add the red pepper.
Process until finely chopped, and then trickle in the olive oil and add the water if the mixture seems too thick.
Store in the fridge, covered with a layer of oil to exclude any air. It can keep up to a month if stored correctly.
Serve as a condiment or use to flavour other dishes.

ing: 1 bouquet garni (bay, parsley, thyme, black pepper)
st: Cut all your vegetables into rough blocks. Warm the oil in a large pot and sautÃ© your vegetables, making sure that they soften, but donât colour.
Top up with cold water and add the bouquet garni.
Bring to the boil and reduce the heat to a simmer. Continuously skim the stock.
Simmer for about 30 minutes.
Strain though a fine sieve, discard the vegetables and cool the stock, before storing it in the refrigerator.
The stock can be reduced by two thirds and frozen in ice trays for general use in all cooking.

ing: extra virgin olive oil, for serving
st: Sift the dry ingredients into a bowl. Gently heat the milk in a saucepan until just warm over a medium heat, then add the water.

Make a well in the middle of the dry ingredients and add the milk and water. Knead on a floured surface for 5 minutes until soft. Place the dough into a greased bowl and cover with a clean tea towel. Place in a warm area and allow to rise until doubled in size.

Heat the oil in a deep saucepan. Roll out a small amount of dough on a floured surface to a thickness of 3 mm. Slice diagonally into pieces using a sharp knife. Fry in very hot oil until puffed and golden. Drain on kitchen paper and season with sea salt. Repeat with the remaining dough.
Serve with the olive oil, balsamic vinegar and crushed chilli.

ing: 3 cm fresh ginger, peeled and chopped
3 cm fresh ginger, peeled and chopped
st: Preheat the oven to 180 Â°C and lightly brush a rimmed baking sheet with oil.
For the meatballs, purÃ©e the spring onions, jalapeÃ±os, garlic, ginger, lemon juice and garam masala in a blender until smooth.
Transfer the mixture to a large bowl and add the mince, egg, yoghurt and salt.
Mix everything until well blended.
Divide the mince mixture into golf ballâ sized portions and place them on the baking sheet.
Drizzle with oil and bake for 15 â 20 minutes until browned and cooked through.
For the curry sauce, heat the oil in a large heavy-based pot over a medium heat.
Add the onions, garlic and ginger and cook for about 8 â 10 minutes, stirring often.
Add all the spices and cook for about 2 minutes, stirring often.
Add the tomatoes, stirring and scraping the residue off the bottom of the pot, and bring to a boil.
Add the salt and 2 cups of water, bring to a boil again, then reduce the heat and simmer for about 25 â 30 minutes until the flavours have infused.
Allow to cool, then transfer to a blender and blend until smooth. Place the sauce back in the pot and add the lemon juice and cayenne pepper.
Gently place the meatballs into the sauce, bring to a simmer and cook for about 5 minutes until they are heated all the way through.
Serve the meatballs and curry sauce topped with the fresh coriander.

ing: a handful fresh mint leaves, finely chopped
500 g red split lentils, rinsed in cold water
5 cm fresh ginger, peeled and finely grated
st: For the minty peas, cook the peas then drain and mash them, and stir in the lemon juice, yoghurt and mint. Mix well and set aside.
To make the fritters, heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a pan and fry the ginger and garlic for 1 minute, then add the spices and curry leaves and fry for another minute.
Add the lentils and 1 litre of water. Bring to a boil then simmer for 25 minutes.
Stir in the coriander and flour then leave to cool.
Shape the mixture into 8 fritters and put them in the fridge for 30 minutes to firm up.
Heat the remaining oil in a pan and fry the fritters, in batches, until browned.
Transfer to paper towels to drain.
Serve the fritters warm with the minty peas.
To make the mayonnaise, combine the peanut butter, mayonnaise and honey in a large bowl and stir well.
Thin the sauce out with the lemon juice, then stir in the paprika and cayenne pepper. Set aside.
Heat the oil in a large pot and fry the potato chips until golden and crisp.
Serve the fries with the mayonnaise, sprinkled with the spring onion.

ing: 1/2  cup roasted and salted peanuts, chopped
1 cup double cream, whipped to stiff peaks
st: Coat a 21 x 11cm loaf pan with non-stick cooking spray and line with wax paper, allowing it to overhang on both the long sides. Set aside.
Melt the chocolate and cool to room temperature.
In a food processor, purÃ©e the bananas until smooth.
Stir the peanut butter into the cooled chocolate until combined, then stir in the banana purÃ©e.
Gently fold in the whipped cream until combined.
Pour the mixture into the prepared pan and top with the chopped peanuts.
Fold the wax paper over the top, wrap tightly in plastic wrap and freeze for at least 3 hours until firm.
To serve, remove the loaf from the pan-run a hot tea towel across the sides and the bottom of the pan if necessary- cut into about 2 cm thick slices and serve immediately.

ing: salt and freshly ground black pepper
st: Heat the oven to 200Â°C.

In a small bowl, mix the fennel seeds, garlic, 2 tablespoons of olive oil, 1 teaspoon of salt and Â¼ teaspoon of black pepper. Rub the mixture over the pork loin, then place it into a large roasting pan.
In a bowl, mix the quartered onions, potatoes, pears, 1 teaspoon of salt, Â¼ teaspoon black pepper and remaining olive oil.
Scatter the onions, potatoes and pears around the pork and roast for about 70 minutes until cooked through.
Transfer the pork to a cutting board and let it rest for at least 5 minutes before slicing.
Serve with the roasted pears and vegetables.

ing: 1 x 5 cm piece ginger, peeled and finely grated
st: Preheat the oven to 175Â°C.
Spray a 22 x 22 x 4.5 cm metal baking pan with non-stick cooking spray.
Combine the flour, baking powder, cinnamon, ginger, salt and allspice in a medium bowl.
Using an electric mixer, beat the butternut, brown sugar, butter, egg, ginger and 1 teaspoon of vanilla extract in a large bowl to blend.
Fold in the flour mixture and Â½ cup of hazelnuts.
Pour the cake mix into the pan, spreading it to the ledges (the layer will be thin).
Bake the cake for about 30 minutes, until a tester inserted into the centre comes out clean. Allow to cool completely.
Bring the cream to a boil in a small saucepan over a medium heat.
Remove from the heat, add the white chocolate and remaining Â¼ teaspoon of vanilla extract and whisk until smooth. Let it stand at room temperature for about 20 minutes until thick enough to spread.
Spread the icing over the thin cake layer. Sprinkle the remaining Â¼ cup of hazelnuts over the top and serve.

ing: to serve raw flaked almonds, toasted
a small handful fresh basil leaves, roughly chopped
2 x 100 g Chevin goat's milk cheese with honey, sliced
salt and freshly ground black pepper
700 g beetroot, peeled, tops and root ends trimmed and cut into wedges
st: Preheat the oven to 200 Â°C.
Spread the beetroot wedges on a baking sheet, drizzle with 2 tablespoons of the olive oil, sprinkle with the thyme and season.
Roast in the oven for 45 minutes until tender.
For the salad dressing, mix the remaining olive oil with the honey, lemon juice and pomegranate concentrate. Season and set aside.
Steam or blanch the broccoli until just tender.
Heat the grill to medium-high.
Place the goatâs cheese on a baking sheet lined with foil, and grill for 2 minutes.
Toss the roasted beetroot in half of the salad dressing.
Toss the broccoli, herbs and dried cranberries in the remaining dressing.
To serve, place the herb leaves on a platter, top with the beetroot and goatâs cheese, and sprinkle with the cranberries and almonds.

ing: 400 g Halloumi cheese, cut lengthwise into thick slices
a small handful fresh thyme, leaves removed and finely chopped
st: In a wide, open bowl, mix the oil, honey, thyme, lemon zest and juice until well blended.
Add the halloumi cheese and set aside to marinate for 15 minutes or overnight in the fridge.
Heat a grill pan over a medium-high heat.
Grill the halloumi cheese for 1 â 2 minutes per side or until browned and bubbling.
Serve immediately sprinkled with olives, Bella tomatoes and red onion slices, and drizzled with any leftover marinade.

ing: 4 fresh thyme sprigs, plus extra for serving
200 g Woolworths Gruberg cheese, thickly sliced
200 g Woolworths Royal Ashton cheese, thickly sliced
sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
st: To make the bÃ©chamel sauce, scald the milk in a saucepan along with the onion, thyme, bay leaf and peppercorns for 3â5 minutes until it starts to simmer. Remove from the heat, strain and set aside.

In a clean saucepan, combine the butter and flour, and cook for 2 minutes, then add the flavoured milk, a splash at a time, whisking continually. Once the sauce has thickened enough to coat the back of a spoon, remove it from the heat and season.
Place a griddle pan over a high heat, brush the bread with olive oil, then chargrill the bread for 1 minute on each side.

Preheat the oven grill. Layer slices of both cheeses and the ham over half of the slices of bread, place on a baking tray and grill. Once the cheese bubbles, remove the tray from the oven and spoon approximately 1 T bÃ©chamel sauce over each slice. Season and sprinkle over the thyme, then grill again until golden brown and bubbling.
Top each slice with the remainingtoast and serve immediately.

ing: 1 box Woolworths gluten-free chocolate brownie mix
st: Ensure all ingredients are at room temperature.
Preheat oven to 180 Â°C. Grease baking tin and line with baking paper.
Pour brownie mix, chocolate chips and pecan nuts into a bowl and make a well in the centre.
Mix oil, milk and eggs together.
Pour into well and mix with a wooden spoon. Mix the batter vigorously for 1 minute, be careful not to over mix.
Spoon the batter into the baking tin. Using the reverse side of the spoon spread the batter into the four corners of the tin.
Bake for 15 to 17 minutes for soft and gooey brownies or 20 to 22 minutes for cake-like brownies.
Remove from the oven and allow cooling for 20 minutes in the pan.
Remove from the pan and cook on cooling rack.
Cut into squares and enjoy.

Preheat the oven to 180Â°C and grease a 15 cm springform baking tin. Whisk the egg yolks and caster sugar together in a glass bowl over a saucepan of simmering water until light and fluffy, taking care not to scramble the egg. Remove from the heat.
Stir the sour cream into the egg mixture and combine well. Sift the coconut flour and the baking powder, then add to the wet ingredients.

Beat the egg whites until stiff peaks form, then gently fold into the cake mixture.Spoon some of the mixture into the baking tin and gently press down to make a layer 2 cm thick. Place a few raspberries on top of the batter and bake for 20 minutes, or until the sides begin to brown and the batter is firm.
Once cooked, remove the cake from the tin and place on a cooling rack. Repeat with the remaining batter to make 5 layers.
Sandwich the layers of cake with the crÃ¨me fraÃ®che icing and cover the sides of the cake with the remaining icing. Garnish with raspberries.
To make the crÃ¨me fraÃ®che icing, whisk together the crÃ¨me fraÃ®che, vanilla powder and raspberries until the icing thickens enough to spread and the berries have burst.

ing: 4 Woolworths ultimate burger buns, cut side lightly toasted
1 tbsp Woolworths black truffle flavoured olive oil
sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
st: Heat the olive oil over a high heat. Shape the mince into 4 patties before seasoning with salt and freshly ground black pepper.
Cook for 3 minutes or until the patty is well caramelized and has developed a crust, turn over and cook the other side in the same manner.

To make the truffle infused, exotic mushroom sauce,heat the oil over a medium heat. Tear the larger mushrooms and add them to the pan along with the smaller mushrooms. Allow the mushrooms to cook and brown without being disturbed before turning over and cooking the other side. Once well browned season with salt and freshly ground black pepper. Pour in the cream and drizzle in the truffle oil before cooking for another 2-3 minutes reducing slightly.

Add the lettuce to the cut side of the buns along with the tomato. Add the burger patty and top with the sliced cheese before spooning the still warm mushroom sauce, causing the cheese to melt slightly.
Spread the Dijon mustard on the remaining bun before topping and serving the burger.

ing: 1 box free from gluten lemon poppy seed muffin mix
st: Prepare the muffin mix according to package instructions.
Bake in the oven at 180 for 20 minutes.
To make the cream cheese icing, simply combine the ingredients.
Ice the muffins to your liking.

ing: lemon, cut into wedges, to serve
300 g Woolworths ready to cook frozen scallops, thawed
450 g Woolworths frozen ready to cook prawns, thawed
60 g Woolworths all pupose gluten free flour
sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
st: Preheat oven to 200Â°C. Drizzle olive oil into a roasting dish before adding the prawns and scallops. Add the butter and garlic and toss together with oregano, chilli flakes, salt and pepper.

Prepare the sauce by heating the butter in a pot over a medium heat. Once melted add the gluten free flour, stir together until combined. Slowly begin adding the milk and stirring through to form a sauce. Gradually start adding the cheese while continuing to stir to prevent any cheesy lumps forming.
Pour the cheese over the seafood before placing under the grill to cook for 10 minutes or until the cheese sauce has slightly gratinated and the seafood is cooked.

Prepare the pasta by starting the garlic in a pan with the olive oil over a medium heat. Add the chilli flakes, and parsley before tossing the cooked pasta through then adding to a serving dish. Spoon the seafood mixture with the cheese sauce over the pasta and serve with a few basil leaves and lemon wedges on the side.
Place all the ingredients in a food processor and pulse until mixture comes together and is sticky.
Line a loaf tin with baking paper, then sprinkle with half the sesame seeds.
Press mixture into the tin, then sprinkle the rest of the sesame seeds on top.
Slice the mixture into bars.
Wrap bars in wax paper and store in an airtight container.

ing: 500 g Woolworths fiorelli, prepared as per the instructions
2 x 105 g Woolworths mascarpone with basil pesto and sweet tomato
350 g exotic tomatoes, halved and quartered
st: Heat the olive oil over a medium heat. Add the garlic and chilli followed by the marrow, and tomatoes. Allow the vegetable to sautÃ© and char slightly.
In a separate bowl combine the mascarpone and lemon juice. In a large mixing bowl toss together the cooked vegetables, pasta and mascarpone.
Add to a serving platter before topping with the croutons, fresh basil and a drizzle of extra virgin olive oil.

ing: vine tomatoes, blistered on the grill
2 x 800 g steak, at room temperature
st: To make the smokey barbeque relish, place the onion and garlic in a food processor and process until finely chopped.
Heat the extra virgin olive oil in a medium saucepan over a high heat. Add the onion mixture, bay leaves and chillies and cook, stirring, for â minutes or until the onion is soft.
Add the mustard powder, paprika and sea salt flakes and cook for 30 seconds.

Add the tomatoes, brown sugar, Worcestershire sauce, honey and red wine vinegar and bring to the boil. Reduce the heat to low and cook, stirring occasionally, for 20-25 minutes or until thickened. Discard the bay leaves and chillies and set aside
Preheat a chargrill pan or barbeque to high heat.
Place the peppercorns in a mortar and pound with a pestle until crushed. Add the sea salt flakes and mix to combine.
Drizzle the steaks with the extra virgin olive oil and sprinkle with the peppercorn mixture.
Cook the steaks for 5-6 minutes on each side for medium ârare or until cooked to your liking. Set aside to rest for 5 minutes.
To serve, slice the steaks and serve with the smokey barbeque relish and blistered vine tomatoes.
Heat olive oil, and then pinch tablespoon size chunks of pork bangers out of the casing and roll into balls.
Place meatballs into the pan, and brown on all sides.
Add stock to the meatballs, then simmer until the meatballs are cooked through.
Remove from the heat, then stir in crÃ¨me fraiche and basil, season to taste, then set aside.
In another pan, heat olive oil, then add the garlic and chilli and saute for a minute.
Add the marrow spaghetti, then stir fry for a few minutes until the spaghetti begins to soften.
Season to taste then place into serving bowls.
Spoon the meatballs and sauce over the spaghetti, then sprinkle with parmesan cheese to serve.

ing: Biscotti or amaretti biscuits, for serving
4 cups Italian ground coffee, freshly brewed
st: Place a scoop of ice cream into 4 cups and pour over the hot coffee.
Drizzle with a tot of almond liquer if you like. Serve with the biscuits.
Cook's note: If you have the time, place the cups containng the ice cream in the freezer for 30 minutes before pouring over the coffee. The biscuits can also be crumbled over.
Fun Fact: "Affogato" means "drowned" in Italian. This recipe is the classic version but if you want to experiment, use coffee, chocolate or stracciatella ice cream.
Shred the chicken, discarding the skin and bones.
SautÃ© onion, chorizo, carrot and aubergine.
Cook until onions are translucent and the vegetables are tender.
Add cumin, coriander and cinnamon.
Mix to combine.
Add the chicken stock and saffron.
Simmer gently until liquid is reduced by half.
Mix in the chicken, chopped parsley and ground almonds.
Remove from the heat.
Brush a spring form cake tin with some of the melted butter.
Lay in the 1st sheet of pastry - making sure that it comes up the sides of the cake tin and flaps over the rim of the tin.
Brush the pastry with butter.
Repeat the process with 3 more sheets of pastry.
Spoon the chicken mixture into the pastry-lined tin, making sure to press down and pack it tightly.
Top with the final pastry sheet, tucking it into the edges to fit.
Fold the overlapping pieces of pastry loosely over the top and brush with more butter.
Sprinkle with salt then place into the oven and bake for 30 minutes until golden brown and crispy.
Remove the pie from the cake tin.
Serve.

ing: 1 kg frozen mashed potatoes, prepared as per instructions
100 g cashew nuts, toasted and roughly chopped
4 tbsp coriander, roughly chopped, extra for garnishing
450 g frozen ready to cook prawns
st: Heat the oil over a medium heat. Add the curry paste and cook for 2 minutes or until fragrant.
Add the coconut milk and bring to a simmer.
Add the frozen prawns and cook until the prawns are almost tender
Add the frozen greens and cook for another 4 minutes
Make the mashed potatoes as per package instructions
Season the curry with fish sauce
Garnish with the coriander and cashew nuts
Serve over Woolies mashed potatoes and a twist and a lime on the side.
Sign in/Register

ing: sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
1 papaya, cubed or cut into wedges
sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
st: Preheat the oven to 200Â°C.

Place the 800 g fish on a greased baking tray and season to taste. Dot with 2 tbsp butter and drizzle with 2 tbsp extra virgin olive oil. Grill the fish for 5 minutes on each side, or until cooked through.
Place the  cubed papaya and 80 g watercress in a mixing bowl with the 30 g picked coriander, 35 g microherbs, 1 juiced lemon and remaining 2 tbsp olive oil.
Serve the fish topped with the papaya-and-watercress salad, with the chermoula aÃ¯oli on the side.

To make the chermoula aÃ¯oli, place the 4 egg yolks and 2 tsp Dijon mustard in a mixing bowl and whisk while slowly pouring in the 1 1/2 cups of oil. Keep whisking until the oil-and-yolk mixture has increased in volume and turned pale in colour. Add the 1 juiced lemon and season to taste. Add the remaining ingredients (1 tbsp turmeric, 1 tbsp smoked paprika, 1 tsp dried chilli flakes, 2 finley chopped garlic cloves and 1 x 4 cm finely grated piece of ginger)and combine. Serve with the grilled hake.
Preheat oven to 200Â°C.
Place butter and oil into individual baking dishes then place into the oven for 3 minutes to heat up.
In a bowl, whisk together the eggs, milk, flour and sugar until smooth.
Remove from the oven and swirl to coat the pan in the oil and butter.
Quickly pour in the batter and return to the oven immediately.
Bake for about 15 minutes or until the sides have puffed up and the edges are golden and crisp â do NOT open the oven during cooking as this will cause the pancake to collapse.
Sprinkle castor sugar over the nectarines and leave to sit for 5 minutes.
Heat a griddle pan, then grill the nectarines until caramelized on the edges.
Place the nectarines into the center of the pancake, scatter over some blueberries, top with a dollop of crÃ¨me fraiche and a drizzle of honey â serve immediately.

t: Greens with vino cotto and tzatziki
st: Bring a large pot of salted water to the boil. Blanch the asparagus, baby pak choi and broccoli for 20â30 seconds, or until just tender.
Blanch the peas and mangetout in the same way for 1 minute and the Brussels sprouts for 3 minutes.
Cook the washed leeks in simmering salted water for 10 minutes, drain, then transfer to a serving bowl and add the blanched vegetables.
Drizzle over the dressing, toss and serve with the tzatztiki. Garnish with mint.
Blend the yoghurt and frozen bananas, then place in a bowl and freeze for 1 hour. Do the same with the berries.
Remove from the freezer, mix the two and freeze once more until set.
Coat the garlic head with the olive oil and roast in a 180Â°C oven for 40 minutes to 1 hour until the garlic is soft.
Place the milk in a pot and warm to scalding point.
Cut the head in half and squeeze the sweet garlic into the milk.
Add the beans (rinsed and drained) and the thyme and cook the mixture on a low heat for about 10 minutes.
Remove the thyme sprigs and place the beans in a blender, or blend with a hand blender to a smooth puree.
Pass the puree through a sieve to ensure that there are no lumps.
If the consistency is too thick you can add a bit more milk. Season and reheat to serve with the rosemary ribeye roast.

ing: 50 g raw unsalted almonds in their skin, toasted
st: Melt the chocolate for 1 minute in the microwave and stir to make sure the mixture is smooth.
Add the toasted almonds to the chocolate and coat them well.
Remove the nuts individually from the chocolate and place on a silicone mat or baking paper sprayed with baking spray.
Carefully place a salt crystal or chilli flake on each nut.
Place them in the fridge for about 30 minutes to set.
Keep in a cool area until ready to serve.

ing: Sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
Sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
1 tbsp olive oil, plus extra for moistening
st: Preheat the oven to 220Â°C.
Moisten the beef with olive oil and sear in a pan, then transfer to a roasting pan.
Mix the olive oil, Worcester sauce and seasoning and coat the beef. Roast for 15 minutes. Wrap the meat in foil and rest.
Serve the beef thinly sliced with the Yorkshire pudding, gravy and watercress.
To make the gravy, pour the Port into the roasting pan and simmer. Stir in the mustard and stock and simmer. Season to taste.
To make the Yorkshire pudding, whisk the eggs, then add the milk and water. Sift in the flour and salt and whisk until smooth. Chill for 30 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 220Â°C. Grease a square baking pan with the oil and heat in the oven until smoking hot. Whisk the batter, then pour into the pan. Bake for 25 minutes.

t: Gammon with caramel apples and fennel
ing: Sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
4 Pink Lady apples, cored and quartered
2 kg Woolworths ready to cook medium gammon
st: Roast the gammon according to package instructions. Allow to rest before slicing.

Place the apples in a skillet, dot with butter and sugar and toss in the pan for 10 minutes over smouldering coals or on the hob until the sugar starts to form a loose caramel and starts to stick to the apples.
Marinate the fennel in the lemon juice and olive oil and serve with the sliced gammon and apples.
Place the blue cheese between two sheets of plastic wrap and roll out carefully to four times its size.
Cut the rolled-out cheese in half and remove the top layer of plastic wrap.
Place one half, plastic side down, into a small tray or dish.
Spread the frozen yoghurt evenly over the cheese.
Place the remaining layer of cheese, with the plastic wrap facing up, onto the yoghurt and press down.
Freeze for 15 to 20 minutes.
To serve: Remove from the freezer and turn out onto a clean board. Using a heart-shaped cookie-cutter, cut out and place onto plates. Serve with fresh cherries or berries.

ing: Sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
st: Preheat the oven to 200Â°C.

Using a pastry brush, generously spread the butter over eight of the phyllo-pastry sheets before layering one on top of the other. Cut 10 cm-wide panels of the pastry and arrange a portion of the goatâs cheese at one end of each panel, topped with a few tomato slices.
Fold the remaining pastry over the cheese and tomato and again top with cheese and tomato. Repeat until you are left with a tall stack, then repeat with the other pastry panels.
Transfer to a baking tray and bake for 15 minutes, or until the pastry is crisp and golden.
Crush the olives in the olive oil and liberally spoon over the hot oozing goatâs cheese-and-tomato phyllo stacks. Season to taste and serve immediately.

ing: 8x150 g Woolworths Italian Gorgonzola, at room temperature
st: Place the Gorgonzola in a mixing bowl and mix using a wooden spoon.
Line a 22-cm springform cake tin with clingwrap and fill with the cheese. Press down to compact. Freeze for 1 hour.
To make the frosting, melt the white chocolate and cultured cream in a bowl over a saucepan of simmering water.
Remove from the cake tin and place on a cake stand. Spread over the frosting.
Top with a golden toffee apple and drizzle with fynbos honey.

ing: Woolworths bulk papaya & berry fruit salad
Woolworths Spring drinks of any variety and size (enough to fill the bowls you're using)
st: Fill a large plastic or freezer friendly bowl halfway with the Woolies spring drink, add the mint and berries before placing a slightly smaller bowl inside the larger bowl, creating somewhat of a mold.
Secure the bowl be either using strong tape or place a can or object inside the small bowl to hold it down slightly.
Place in the freezer over night.
Once set and completely frozen remove the inner bowl then remove the frozen bowl from the large bowl. Fill with the fruit picnic selection and serve.
Note you can also fill the frozen bowls with Woolies fruit nectars and serve with as a frozen glass.

ing: Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
st: Peel and dice vegetables into 1cm cubes. Season the fish with salt and pepper.
Heat some of the olive oil in a frying pan. Place the salmon in the pan, skin side up, and fry of approximately 3 minutes on each side.
While still pink inside, remove and keep warm. Add the diced root vegetables, except the beetroot which you should do separately, to the remaining oil and roast gently for about 8 â 10 minutes.

Season and keep warm next to the salmon. Deglaze the pan with the white wine and reduce for 3 minutes. Add the sour cream. Simmer for another 3 minutes. Season to taste and add the lemon thyme leaves at the last minute.

Put some root vegetables in the centre of a dinner plate. Place the salmon on top of the vegetables and pour a little sour cream sauce on the fish and around the plate. Garnish with a small sprig of lemon thyme. Serve with a glass of crisp white wine.

ing: enough extra virgin olive oil to form a chunky sauce
salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
extra virgin olive oil, to drizzle
semolina to line the oven tray
st: Grease a large oven tray before coating with the semolina. Stretch the dough to fit in the tray.
Top the dough with the tomato chutney before adding the toppings, allow the dough to rest for 30 minutes to rise.
Drizzle the olive oil over before placing in the oven to cook for 30-40 minutes at 180 or until the dough is perfectly cooked and the toppings are slightly charred.
Spoon over some of the herbed olive dressing and serve immediately.

ing: 4 cups vanilla ice cream, slightly softened but not melted
130 g dark chocolate enrobed marzipan, coursley chopped
st: Preheat the oven to 180 Â°C.
Line two 33 cm x 23 cm baking trays with foil, extending it over the sides. Spray the foil with cooking spray, and set aside.
Crack the eggs into a large bowl and add the cocoa powder, salt, baking powder and vanilla extract. Beat with an
electrical hand mixer until smooth.

Place the butter in a medium saucepan over a medium heat, and stir as the butter melts. Add the sugar and stir just until the sugar dissolves, gets glossy and bubble start to appear. Donât let the butter boil.
Take the pan off the heat, add the hot butter to the egg mixture and mix until smooth. Add the flour and mix again until the flour is incorporated.
Divide the batter between the two baking trays and spread into even layers.
Bake for 14 â 15 minutes, until the edges start pulling away from the sides of the pan. Allow to cool on a wire rack for about 15 minutes, then refrigerate until chilled.
Spray a 33 cm x 23 cm tray with cooking spray and line with a layer of plastic wrap, extending it over the sides.
Mix the dark chocolate enrobed marzipan pieces into the vanilla ice cream.
Spoon into the prepared tray and freeze for at least 1 hour, until firm.
Remove the ice cream from the pan, using the plastic wrap as handles. Flip it upside down onto one brownie layer in its pan. Remove the plastic wrap.

Remove the second brownie layer from its pan, peel the foil off and slide it on top of the ice cream. Press the brownie layer gently so it adheres to the ice cream. Freeze for at least 30 minutes, until the brownie layers are firm enough to cut cleanly. Remove the layered brownies and ice cream from the pan using the foil as handles. Use a large, sharp knife to cut 12 ice cream sandwiches. Leave at room temperature for 5 minutes before serving.
Place the 1 cup cream in a small saucepan over a high heat and bring to a boil.
Place the 600 g finely chopped 70 % dark chocolate in a medium heatproof bowl and top with the hot cream.
Place the bowl over a saucepan of simmering water and, using a metal spoon, stir until melted and smooth.
Allow to stand at room temperature for 10 minutes.
Stir in the crumbled 400 g fruit cake until well combined.
Refrigerate for 2 â 3 hours or until just firm.
Roll teaspoonfuls of the mixture into balls and place on a large baking tray lined with non-stick baking paper. Refrigerate for 15 minutes or until set.
Place the 200 g finely chopped 70 % dark chocolate and 2 tsp vegetable oil in a medium heatproof bowl over a saucepan of simmering water and, using a metal spoon, stir until melted and smooth.

Insert a toothpick into a fruit cake ball, and dip it in the melted chocolate, allowing any excess chocolate to drip off. Once all have been dipped, stick the other ends of the toothpicks into a piece of thick cardboard.
Refrigerate for 30 minutes or until set. Remove the truffles from the toothpicks to serve.

t: Grilled fish with green spelt salad
ing: extra virgin olive oil, to drizzle over and coat
st: Coat the  x 150 g hake fillets in some olive oil before spooning over the 4 tbsp salt free seasoning and coating well. Place on an oven tray to cook at 200Â°C for about 7 minutes a side or until the fish is slightly charred outside and perfectly cooked inside.

For the green spelt salad: Add the2 x 150 g spelt to a large mixing bowl along with the chopped herbs (4 tbsp parsley, 2 tbsp mint, 4 tbsp basil), 4 tbsp roughly chopped olives and 2 tbsp salt free seasoning.
Toss together with the freshly squeezed lemon juice and lemon zest. Serve with the fresh also served with fresh lemon juice squeezed over.
Line a baking sheet with baking paper then pour on the dark chocolate
Drizzle the white chocolate onto the dark chocolate, then using a toothpick, make a swirled pattern on the chocolate.
Break up the cookies into halves and quarters, then place onto the chocolate, pressing down to secure.
Sprinkle on some cinnamon, then leave to set in the fridge.
Cut the bark into pieces, serve with coffee after dinner or give to friends as gifts

ing: Woolworths Christmas shaved brussel sprouts and cranberry salad with lemon dressing and festive sprinkles
Sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
2 x 150 g Woolworths tenderstem asparagus and broccoli packs
400 g Woolworths pork rashers, cut into cubes
st: Add the cubed pork to a cold pan before placing over a medium heat. Allow the fat to render out while tossing to crispy evenly. Add the olive oil, Brussels sprouts and tenderstem vegetables. Allow the vegetable to coat in the oil and cook until slightly charred but cooked until tender.

Season with salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste. Ad the Woolies Brussels sprouts salad mix to a large mixing bowl before adding the cooked vegetables and tossing with the dressings provided.
Steam or blanch the 600g tenderstem broccoli until bright green and tender.
Meanwhile, make the dressing by whisking together all of the ingredients (2 tsp wholegrain mustard, juice of 1 orange, handful chopped parsley, Â¼ cup olive oil, 1 tsp sugar, salt and pepper.
Pour the dressing onto the broccoli and toss well before arranging on a platter.
Sprinkle on the100 g toasted almonds.

ing: Woolworths peanut butter filled pretzels, to top
Woolworths UHT real dairy cream, to top
Woolworths chocolate dessert sauce, to drizzle
1 L Woolworths tinroof ice cream, extra for the stroop waffles
st: Add a scoop of the ice cream to one of the stroopwaffles before topping with another to create a sandwich. Roll the sides into the popping candy. Keep in the freezer until its needed.
Drizzle the chocolate sauce along the inside of an oversized glass then do the same with the caramel sauce.

In a blender, blend together the milk and tin roof ice cream before pouring into the glasses, Squeeze over the cream. Add the stroopwaffle sandwich to the side of the glass along with the marshmallow and sprinkling of peanut butter filled pretzels. Drizzle over extra caramel and chocolate sauce before toasting the marshmallow with a burner and finishing off with a Santa chocolate lolly and sparklers

ing: 300 g good quality dark chocolate, melted
st: Add any left over fruit cake to a mixing bowl and break up before rolling into small balls. Coating your hands in coconut oil helps mold the balls without getting it stuck on your hands.
Add the brownie mince pies to a bowl and break apart. Shape these into the same sized balls as well.
Using a skewer: Skewer the balls before dipping into the chocolate. Carefully place on a dish.
Top some of the still wet chocolate with coconut, some with sesame, orange zest and some with flaked salt.
Allow the chocolate to set before packaging or serving,

ing: 1 clove garlic, peeled and finely chopped
1 x 400 g chickpeas, drained and rinsed
1 avocado, cut in half and skin and stone removed
st: Blend all the ingredients in a food processor until smooth.
Transfer the avocado hummus to a bowl and cover with cling film.
Chill in the fridge for one hour.
Serve with warm flatbread, or use as a dip or spread. Serve with a healthy salad or in a wrap, also delicious as a pasta or pizza sauce.

ing: olive oil, for drizzling, to serve
balsamic vinegar, for drizzling, to serve
3 tbsp Italian parsley, roughly chopped, to serve
st: Cook the bacon in a medium-sized pan over a medium-heat, stirring occasionally for about 5 minutes or until crisp. Leave to cool on paper towels, then crumble.
Bring the honey and 2 tablespoons of water to a boil in the same pan as the bacon.
Add the grapes and chilli flakes. Cook for about 5 minutes or until the grapes are glazed and starts to soften.
Mix in the bacon and season to taste.
Spread the toasts with the feta and top with the grape mixture. Sprinkle with the chopped parsley and drizzle with the olive oil and balsamic cream.

ing: extra virgin olive oil, for drizzling
st: Cook the bacon in a medium-sized pan over a medium-heat, stirring occasionally for about 5 minutes or until crisp. Leave to cool on paper towels, then crumble.
Bring the honey and 2 tablespoons of water to a boil in the same pan as the bacon.
Add the grapes and chilli flakes. Cook for about 5 minutes or until the grapes are glazed and starts to soften.
Mix in the bacon and season to taste.
Spread the toasts with the feta and top with the grape mixture. Sprinkle with the chopped parsley and drizzle with the olive oil and balsamic cream.

ing: sea salt and freshly ground pepper, to taste
1 x 350 g woolworths roasting vine tomatoes
st: Slice the strawberries and tomatoes into chunks. Shave the fennel bulb into wafer-thin slices using a vegetable peeler or slice very thinly using a sharp knife. Toss with the strawberries and tomatoes. Dress with the olive oil, red wine vinegar and season to taste.
Heat a nonstick pan over a medium heat, then dry-fry the halloumi for 30 seconds on each side, or until golden brown. Remove from the pan and dot onto the salad. Top with micro-herbs and fresh basil.

ing: sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
2 x 200 g tuna steaks, thinly sliced
4 green mangoes, peeled and thinly sliced
st: Cut the mango slices into thin matchstick-sized strips. Place in a bowl and combine with the soy and fish sauces, rice-wine vinegar and a squeeze of lemon or lime juice.
Arrange the avocado wedges on four plates and top with the sliced tuna and mango salad. Spoon the pulp from the granadillas onto each plate and scatter with chives. Season to taste.
Place the fruit on a tray and sprinkle with the sugar, vanilla seeds and cinnamon. Braai over hot coals or grill in a griddle pan for 3 minutes on each side. Set aside.
To make the coulis, place all the ingredients in a saucepan and bring to a boil. Simmer for 7 minutes, skimming off the foam, or until thick. Transfer to a jug and cool.
Arrange the fruit on plates, drizzle over the coulis and serve with the sorbet.

ing: salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
st: Chargrill the red pepper under the oven grill
Place in a bowl covered in cling wrap and leave to sweat for 15 minutes
Peel off the blackened skin, slice open and remove the seeds
Place the flesh in a blender
Add chickpeas, thyme, paprika, cumin, garlic, chilli, lemon zest, lemon juice, tahini, seasoning and yoghurt
Blitz to make hummus
Set aside
Place the eggs into a pot, then cover with cold water.
Place the pot onto the heat, then bring to the boil, and leave to boil for 5 minutes.
Remove from the heat, then leave the eggs to sit in the hot water for another 5 minutes.
Drain, then rinse the eggs under cold water to cool completely.
Peel the eggs, then cut into halves and scoop out the yolk and place into a bowl, place the whites onto a serving platter.
Mash the yolks, then mix in the mayonnaise, sweet chilli sauce, chives and cayenne, then season well.
Spoon the mixture back into the egg whites, or place the mixture into a piping bag and pipe.
Slice the bacon into lardons, then cook in a hot pan until crisp.
Sprinkle the bacon bits over the eggs before serving.

ing: 1 pineapple, peeled and wedged into four pieces
st: Heat 4 T runny honey and 2 T butter in the microwave.
Brush onto peeled wedges of pineapple and chargrill in a griddle pan for 3â5 minutes on each side.
Serve hot with ice cream or crÃ¨me fraÃ®che

ing: left over slices of roast beef or grilled steak, sliced
maldon salt and pepper, to taste
st: Heat a non-stick frying pan over medium to high heat. Fry the garlic and thyme in the butter and olive oil for 1 minute, until golden.
Add the torn mushrooms and cook for 4 minutes. Add the cream and continue cooking for 2 minutes.
Add the left over meat and season.

ing: 600 g fresh angelfish, skinned and filleted
sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
2 firm ripe red tomatoes, finely chopped
1 red chilli, seeded and finely chopped
st: Dust the fish with the chilli powder, sprinkle with oregano and salt and moisten with olive oil.
Pangrill for a few minutes on each side until seared and just cooked. Transfer to a platter.
At the table, wrap the fish in the warmed wraps, adding the cabbage, smashed avocado, tomato salsa, coriander and a squeeze of lime.
To make the smashed avocado, scoop the avocado flesh into a bowl. Add the lime juice, garlic and seasoning. Mash roughly using the back of a spoon.

ing: 600 g fresh angelfish, skinned and filleted

2 firm ripe red tomatoes, finely chopped

ing: 250 g cream cheese at room temperature
4 x 150 g double cream lemon curd yoghurt
st: Mix together the coconut biscuits and the butter, then press into a 20cm pie tin.
Mix together the cream cheese, yoghurt and lemon curd, then gently fold in the whipped cream.
Spoon mixture into the cookie base, then place into the freezer until completely set (a minimum of three hours).
Remove the pie from the freezer 20 minutes before serving, then roughly crush the meringues and scatter onto the pie as a topping.
Slice into wedges to serve.
Preheat the oven to 180Â°C.
Mix 210 g fl our, 1 t bicarbonate of soda, 150 g brown sugar, 55 g caster sugar, 1 free-range egg, 1 t vanilla paste and 175 g melted butter.
Stir in 100 g chopped macadamia nuts, then transfer to a greased 23 cm round cast-iron skillet. Gently press down to level. Gently press 200 g plain chocolate Easter eggs into the mixture.
Bake for last 20 minutes. Enjoy warm right out of the skillet topped with vanilla ice cream.
Preheat your oven to 180C. Butterfly the lamb being careful not to cut through the flesh.
In a blender combine the rosemary, garlic, salt, pepper, spring onion, 3/4 cup of olive oil and vinegar. Blend to form a pourable sauce.
Cover the lamb with the sauce before massaging into the meat and setting aside to marinade overnight or at least for 15 minutes.
Roll the meat up and secure with butchers twine. Cover the outside of the lamb with the leftover sauce and place on a roasting tray.
Place the lamb in the oven to roast for 1 and a half hours to 2 hours depending on how you prefer your doneness.
Carve the lamb and serve it with the spelt salad and roasted vegetables.
Whisk together eggs with milk and double cream.
Add spices and vanilla
Soak your bread slices until they are fully soaked and have absorbed the liquid
Preheat the pan - with sunflower oil
Fry slices of soaked-bread individually
Spread peanut butter on both top and bottom slices
Slice bananas lengthways, lay on the bottom slice (on top of the peanut butter topping)
Add the top slice of French Toast and viola!

Wrap the frikkadel in bacon before securing with a toothpick to ensure it doesnât fall off during cooking. Heat a griddle pan over a high heat and add the frikkadels to cook for about 3 minutes a side to get perfect charred lines on it.
Ensure the bacon is perfectly cook, the frikkadel can be cooked to medium well.

ing: salt and freshly ground black pepper
st: Prepare the frikkadels as instructed.

For the pap chips: Bring the water to a simmer with the salt and butter before adding the pap and stirring to prevent any lumps.After stiring for about 5 minutes the pap should become slightly thick. Pour it into a greased rectangle dish and place in the fridge to set.Heat the oil over a medium heat. Turn the pap out and cut into chip like shapes before adding to the oil and cooking for about 1 minute a side to ensure theyâre golden and crisp.

For the lemony spinach: Heat the oil over a medium heat before adding the swiss chard and wilting down. Add the garlic, lemon zest and juice and season with salt and freshly ground black pepper. After about 3 minutes the spinach should be ready, Serve with the frikkadels and pap chips.

ing: salt and freshly ground black pepper
st: Heat the oil over a high heat. Shape the mince into 2 patties before adding to the pan. Season with salt and freshly ground black pepper.
Cook the patties for about 3 minutes a side and set aside.
For the beer cheese:Blend together until the mixture just comes together, you might only need half a can of beer

Preheat your oven to 220C. Once youâve made your beer cheese spoon about 3 tablespoons of the mixture over the patties. Place the patties in the oven to heat through and melt the cheese. While the patties are in the oven prepare the buns by adding lettuce to the base followed by the pickles and crispy pork rashers and onion marmalade.
Place the cheese topped patties over the onion marmalade and add another small amount of onion marmalade to complement the cheese before topping with the bun tops and serving.

ing: sea salt and feshly ground pepper
st: In a blender, combine the olives with the olive oil and parsley to form a loose paste.
Spread the paste on the pita breads and pile on the radish, watercress, eggs and chives.
Season to taste.
Preheat oven to 180Â°C.
Heat 15 ml of oil and add 1 tsp ground cumin and 1/2 tsp chili flakes. Simmer to release flavour.
Add bolognaise sauce and black beans (drained). Simmer for 5 minutes.
Fill flat breads with sauce, roll and place in a baking dish.
Pour salsa over, sprinkle with cheese and bake for 15â20 minutes.

ing: 400 g jar mild jalapeno & cilantro salsa
400 g tin black beans in brine
st: Place the mince in a pan and fry off.
Once browned, add the diced tinned tomatoes and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the kidney beans, heat through and season well.
Heat wrap as per instructions.
To assemble, place the wrap on a plate, on one side of the wrap place the mince, bean and tomato mix. Place 2 teaspoons of the jalapeno salsa on the  mince. Roll the wrap tightly and serve warm.

ing: 375 g Easy to Cook Bright & Crunchy Stir Fry Mix 375g
375 g crisp and crunchy stir fry mix
250 g Carb Cleverâ¢ Spinach & Cauliflower Noodles 250g
100 g sweet and sour stri fry sauce
st: In a wok or large-based saucepan, heat 15ml olive oil on a medium-high heat.
Add the chicken breasts and brown for 2 minutes, then remove from the wok or saucepan.
Add the remaining olive oil and fry the garlic, ginger and stir fry mix vegetables for 5-10 minutes.
Add the noodles and the browned chicken to the pan, along with the stir fry sauce, and cook for an extra 3-5 minutes or until the noodles are cooked.
Season to taste, garnish with picked coriander leaves and serve
Beat 8 free-range eggs with the seeds of 1 vanilla pod and 4 T sugar.
Heat 1 T canola oil in a nonstick pan over a medium heat.
Soak 4 slices sourdough bread in the egg for 2 minutes, then fry the egg-soaked bread for 3 minutes on each side.
Slice 400 g strawberries and mix with 4 T rose-water, 4 T water and 2 T caster sugar. Steep for 5 minutes, then spoon over the French toast.
Dust with icing sugar.

ing: Carb Cleverâ¢ Almond and Seed Bar
st: Beat the eggs and gradually add the sugar.
Add half of the milk and the butter to the egg mixture and stir well.
Sift the flour, baking powder and salt together and add to the egg mixture.
Gradually stir in the remaining milk to form a smooth mixture.
Fold in the cooked quinoa.
Drop a spoonful of batter onto a greased heavy-bottom frying pan.
Turn the flapjack once the top is full of air bubbles and bake on the other side. Repeat using up the remaining batter.
Stack the flapjacks on top of each other and top with strawberries and the broken-up seed bar.
Drizzle with some honey and lime zest.

ing: 1 400 g can butter beans, drained and mashed
Sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
250 g plain cream cheese tubs, at room temperature
st: Place the seed mix in a bowl and keep aside.
Place the dates on a chopping board and remove the pips. Chop the dates finely, mix into the seed mixture and drained beans until well combined and sticky.
Press the seed mixture into the bottom of a 20 cm tart dish to form a base.
Heat a grill pan until very hot. Brush the broccoli and leeks with some olive oil and chargrill until slightly softer.
Add the cream cheese to the base and lay the TenderstemÂ® and leeks on top.
Top with the chopped almonds and drizzle with some olive oil.
Cut the chicken breasts fillets into 2cm x 2cm pieces
Place a non-stick pan on high heat, add 1 tablespoon olive oil and fry the chicken pieces for eight minutes.
Add the salsa and cook for another five min.
Remove from heat and season to taste
Heat up the tortillas by following the packaging instructions
Place the chicken mixture in the middle of the tortilla together with the coleslaw and a dollop of guacamole. Roll and enjoy.

ing: 400 g free range skinless chicken mini breast fillets
140 g sun-dried tomato stir through pasta sauce
st: Fill a pot with 1L of water, add 1tsp salt and bring to a boil
Add pasta, allowing it to cook for 5 minutes until soft. Drain and set aside
On high heat, fry chicken fillets in 1 tsp olive oil for 5 min or until golden brown
Add black olives and cook for another 2 minutes. Set aside
To assemble, add the cooked pasta and chicken to a serving bowl, mix in grated hard cheese, sun-dried tomato pasta sauce and season with salt and pepper.

ing: sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
For the cucumber and fennel salad:
st: Drizzle the lemon dressing over the cucumber and fennel and set aside.

Coat the fish in the spicy coconut sauce. Wrap each portion in nori, then in tinfoil. Grill on the braai for 5â10 minutes, or until tender. Open one of the parcels to make sure the fish is cooked through and flakes easily.

Serve with the cucumber-and-fennel salad, topped with sesame seeds.Cook's note:Take your fish to the next level by dipping it in an Asian-inspired sauce, then wrapping it in sheets of nori, followed by tinfoil to make sure the fish stay nice and juicy. The look on everyone's faces when you unwrap the foil at the table? Priceless.

t: Double beef burger with sriracha mayo
ing: 1/2 cup Clark's hot sticky plum sauce
st: Preheat the oven to 180Â°C.
Break up the patties and reshape into 4 large patties.

Heat the butter and oil in a large ovenproof pan and cook the patties for 5 minutes on each side, or until cooked through. Pour in the plum sauce, transfer to the oven and roast for 10 minutes, or until done to your liking.
Top each patty with 2 slices of cheese.
Spread the sriracha mayo onto the bottom halves of the rolls. Mix the mayonnaise and horseradish and spread onto the top halves of the rolls.

Place a patty on the bottom halves of the rolls, then add the lettuce, tomato, pesto, onion and gherkins and the top halves of the rolls.Cook's note:The perfect burger is all about the balance between a juicy patty, the perfect texture, crunch and flavour.
Preheat the oven to 120Â°C.
Using an electric mixer with the whisk attachment, beat the egg whites until foamy.
Gradually add the caster sugar and beat until the mixture is glossy and stiff peaks form.
Spoon the meringue mixture onto baking trays lined with greaseproof paper and bake for 3 hours or until crispy and dry on the outside.
Arrange the meringues on a plate to resemble a wreath and sprinkle with pistachios. Serve with brown butter ice cream or coconut yoghurt, raspberries and coconut shavings.
Preheat the oven to 180Â°C.
Heat 15 ml of oil in a pan and chicken mini breast fillets, 1 tsp ground cumin and 1/2 tsp chilli flakes.
Simmer to release flavour. Once browned, add the mild chunky salsa and simmer for 10 min, then add black beans and heat through.
Place wrap into an oven dish, fill with the chicken fillets mixture and roll tightly. Repeat for as many burritos as you need.
Top with more salsa and cheese, then bake in the oven for 15-20 minutes.

ing: Sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
st: Mix the yeast and sugar with the water, then set aside for a few minutes.

Turn the flour out onto a clean surface or place in a large bowl. Make a well in the middle and pour in the yeast mixture. Using a fork or blunt knife, slowly stir the liquid into the flour to make a dough.
Knead well for 10 minutes, or until smooth and springy. Cover and set aside until doubled in size. Tear off balls of dough, arrange on a baking tray and leave to rise again until ready to bake.
Preheat the oven to 200Â°C.
Roll out each piece of dough into a thin oval pizza base, drizzle with olive oil and season. Bake for 10 minutes until just light golden.
Melt the honey and butter in a pan, then add the plums cut side down and caramelise while the pizza bakes.
Remove the pizza bases from the oven, tear over the Gorgonzola and prosciutto and add the slightly caramelised plums. Return to the oven and bake until cooked through, about 10 minutes.
Serve warm drizzled with chilli oil and garnished with microherbs.

t: Fried pork chops with burnt sage butter
st: Season the pork loin chops with sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste and pan-fry in olive oil over a medium to high heat for 3â4 minutes a side.
Add the butter to the pan for the last 2â3 minutes of cooking. Cook until the butter is melted and bubbling.
Add a small bunch of fresh sage and cook until the sage is crisp and the butter is dark golden brown.

ing: 2.5 kg Woolworths bone-in smoked large gammon
2 tsp Woolworths Lazy Kettle hickory liquid smoke
st: Preheat the oven to 180Â°C. To make the BBQ sauce, place all the ingredients into a saucepan and simmer for 10 minutes, or until thickened.
Place the gammon on a large baking tray and remove the skin. Score the fat using a sharp knife, taking care not to cut the meat.

Rub the BBQ sauce onto the gammon, then layer the sliced pineapple on top. Pour the honey over the pineapple, then place the gammon in the oven and roast for 1 hour, or until golden and warmed through.

ing: Sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
1 tbsp fresh rosemary finely chopped, plus an additional sprig
st: Preheat the oven 220Â°C. Place 3 T oil in a roasting tray and heat in the oven. Once the oil is hot, add the oxtail and toss until all the meat is coated. Season to taste.
Return the meat to the oven and cook for a further 20 minutes, or until itâs nicely browned and the fat is golden.
Meanwhile, place the carrots, celery and herbs in a large saucepan with the remaining olive oil and gently simmer for 20 minutes. (You may need to add a few tablespoons of water at some point.)

Remove the oxtail from the oven and set aside. Reduce the ovenâs temperature to 170Â°C. Add the bay leaves, cloves, flour, tomatoes, wine and beef stock to the vegetables. Lastly add the oxtail, all the roasting juices and bring to a boil.

Return to the roasting tray, cover with a lid and cook in the oven for a further 5 hours. If you make this a day or two in advance, no harm comes to it if you put it into the oven at 170Â°C for another hour or so to heat it up.

t: Dikuku le gemer (scones and ginger beer)
st: Pour 2 cups of water into a pot. Add sugar and dissolve over a low heat, stirring regularly. Add ginger, cream of tartar, raisins pineapple peel and the rest of the water. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Allow to cool (about an hour) and stir in the yeast. Cover and leave to stand overnight. Strain through a sieve into a 2-litre bottle and chill before serving.
Preheat the oven to 200Â°C and truss the legs of the chicken with string.
Heat the oil in a pan, season the chicken and sear until golden. Transfer to a roasting pan.
Mix the remaining ingredients and pour around the chicken. Braise for 1â11â2 hours, or until golden and tender.
Preheat the grill pan on high heat. Rinse the hake under cold, running water and pat dry with paper towels. Score the fish on both sides. Season with pepper and salt.
Drizzle olive oil on the hot grill and cook the hake for approximately 3 to 4 minutes on each side until crispy and cooked through. Flip carefully so that you do not damage the skin.
Pair grilled fish with ratatouille and preserved lemons served on sliced Ciabatta bread.
Pan-fry 350g green beans in 100g butter, along with 6 sage leaves and a squeeze of lemon juice.
Prepare a tray of our chicken schnitzels and a packet of our Frozen Mashed Potatoes according to the package instructions.
Heat up 200g of our creamy Fresh Mushroom Sauce as per the package instructions.
Serve schnitzels alongside frozen mashed potatoes and green beans stir-fried, with scoops of creamy mushroom sauce

ing: 70  g Pitted black kalamata olives with a hint of herbs
st: Sign in/Register
Preheat oven to 180C
Place the chicken drumstick in oven tray then toss in olive oil and seasoning. Cook in the oven for 30 minute.
Flip the chicken oven in the baking tray then add the chakalaka and cook for a further 30 minutes.
Top with coriander and serve with creamy pap or polenta.
Bake fish as per packaging instructions.
Serve with frozen chips and spinach-filled gem squash, cooked as per packaging instructions.
Prepare the gnocchi as per package instructions and toss through the chilli and garlic sauce.
Serve with stuffed sweet potato, prepared as per package instructions or serve with beetroot, butternut and rocket salad.

ing: 120 g Hot-smoked salmon with pepper, mustard seeds & dill
250 g fresh fettucine, cooked al dente
170 g thin asparagus, trimmed and choped
st: 170 g thin asparagus, trimmed and chopped
1 T olive oil
250 g fresh fettucine, cooked al dente
120 g hot-smoked pepper, mustard and dill salmon flakes
100 g soft goat’s cheese (chevin), crumbled
Sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
Fresh dill sprigs, for sprinkling
Clean and steam the mussels until opened (5 to 10 minutes). Remove top mussel shell and place the remaining half with the mussel itself in an ovenproof pan or baking tray.
Top the mussels with Matboucha sauce.

To make the gratin, mix together the breadcrumbs, grated Parmesan, preserved lemon and chopped parsley. Top the mussels with the crumb mixture and place in the oven under the grill for 5â10 minutes, or until golden.
Serve straight from the oven with fried halloumi, dolmades, a fresh Greek salad and toasted pita breads.
Preheat oven to 180Â°C.
Cream the butter, brown sugar and sugar until pale in colour. Add the maple syrup and egg and whisk until combined.
In a separate bowl, combine the flour, baking powder, salt, ground ginger, ground nutmeg and chocolate chunks.
Form a ball with the dough before covering and placing in the fridge for 30 minutes until firm.
Once the dough has firmed up, begin rolling out 2â 3 cm balls. Spread the extra sugar out in a bowl. Roll the balls of dough in the sugar to coat.
Place the balls on a greased baking tray and flatten slightly before placing in the oven for 12â15 minutes.

To make the crumble, combine the oats, macadamia flour and butter. Using your fingertips, rub together and create a breadcrumb texture. Chill until ready to use. (This is great to prep the night before â you could even make extra, freeze it and use from frozen in the next round).
Slice the stone fruit into thin wedges and add to an oven proof pan with butter. Toss to coat for 5 minutes, add the vanilla and raspberries and remove from the heat.
Sprinkle over your chilled crumble and bake for 35â40 minutes until golden and bubbling. Serve warm with yoghurt, fresh blackberries and a drizzle of honey.

ing: 600 g Woolworths Mature Thick Cut Beef Sirloin Steak
